title: GitHub Release Daily Event Volume
dataSources: GitHub repositories (`github:repo`), commits (`github:commit`), issues (`github:issue`), and releases (`github:release`).
app: GitHub repository metadata, commit activity feeds, issue trackers, and release publish logs forwarded to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=github:release
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as events, dc(repo_name) as distinct_entities by _time
| sort - _time
description: Counts how many GitHub release events land each day and how many distinct repository values are represented.
value: Daily volume is the fastest way to spot a dead feed, a sudden burst, or a workflow that quietly changed.
implementation: Ingest GitHub release records into `index=personal`; schedule daily and compare count and distinct repository values against your normal baseline.
visualization: Column chart of daily event count with a line for distinct entities.
grandmaExplanation: It blends how much GitHub release activity showed up each day so you can see if the feed went quiet or suddenly got busy.
